impact:
Found in T-009 review round 2, chunk 6.

instrument.mjs and net-observe.mjs are handed a log PATHNAME through the environment and append to it from inside the process they observe. That process has ordinary write permission to the file. A hostile in-process dependency can resolve modules outside its root, or attempt egress, then truncate, unlink or replace the log and write one permitted in-root entry. The result satisfies every check the auditors make — non-empty, at least one in-root resolution, buckets that account for every line, a startup sentinel it can read and reproduce — and reads as a clean run.

Chunk 6 closed the observation gaps reachable from inside the process (ESM named-export bypass via syncBuiltinESMExports, fail-open recording, absence-vs-silence ambiguity, constructor semantics). This one is not reachable from inside: capturing the environment value and the fs function once protects neither the file nor its contents.

FIX (architectural, deliberately not half-done during the review round): move the authoritative log where the observed process cannot write. Send observation events to a parent-owned collector over a dedicated pipe/IPC channel rather than a shared path; have the collector, not the child, generate the start/end envelope so an interrupted or missing stream is detectable and not forgeable; reject a run whose event stream is missing, truncated or out of order. Touches instrument.mjs, net-observe.mjs and the conformance/matrix runners that consume the logs. A parent-written sentinel the child can read and reproduce would look like protection without being any.

NOT a blocker for T-009's adopt-v2 verdict: the scripted isolation evidence rests on a dependency closure the supply-chain gate has already refused native-build machinery for, so the adversary described here is not the one the current evidence faces. It is a real weakness in the "silence is evidence" argument and should be closed before that argument is relied on against an untrusted dependency set.
title: Resolution and egress logs live in the observed process's writable namespace
